test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A true-breeding tall pea plant with yellow seeds was crossed with a true-breeding dwarf pea plant with green seeds. In the F1 generation, all the plants were tall. What conclusion can be drawn from this experiment?

options.text: This shows independent assortment of genes.
One parent plant was homozygous, and the other was heterozygous.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Tallness was dominant over dwarfism.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The experiment indicates that the tall trait is dominant over the dwarf trait in pea plants.
 
• Since all F1 generation plants were tall, it suggests that the allele for tallness masks the presence of the allele for dwarfism.
 
• True-breeding tall pea plants are homozygous for the tall allele, while true-breeding dwarf pea plants are homozygous for the dwarf allele.
 
• In the F1 generation, the genotype of the plants would be heterozygous, carrying one allele for tallness and one for dwarfism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **True-breeding**: Organisms that, when bred, produce offspring of the same variety over many generations. This indicates they are homozygous for the trait in question.
 
• **Dominant trait**: A trait that is expressed in the phenotype even when only one copy of the allele is present. In this case, tallness is dominant.
 
• **Recessive trait**: A trait that is masked by the presence of a dominant allele and only expressed phenotypically when two copies of the recessive allele are present. Here, dwarfism is recessive.
 
• **Homozygous**: An organism that has two identical alleles for a trait. True-breeding tall pea plants are homozygous dominant (TT), and true-breeding dwarf pea plants are homozygous recessive (tt).
 
• **Heterozygous**: An organism that has two different alleles for a trait. The F1 generation plants are heterozygous (Tt), having one allele for tallness and one for dwarfism.
 
• **Genotype and Phenotype**: Genotype refers to the genetic makeup of an organism, while phenotype refers to the observable traits. In this case, the genotype Tt results in the phenotype of a tall plant.
